statement: The Newberry Library catalogs the surviving Francisco Ximénez K'iche'/Spanish Popol Vuh manuscript as probably written in 1700–1703; its research guide uses the broader transcription window 1700–1715. These are institutional descriptions of a surviving copy.

sources.citation: Newberry Library Digital Collections, Arte de las tres lenguas kakchiquel, quiché y tzutuhil [vol. 02], Ayer MS 1515, https://collections.newberry.org/archive/-2KXJ8ZSJPW6AI.html
sources.author: Newberry Library
sources.access_note: Catalog states 'probably written between 1700 and 1703'; metadata entry concerning the manuscript, not a page-by-page transcription of its content.

sources.citation: Newberry Library, Popol Vuh research guide, https://www.newberry.org/collection/research-guide/popol-vuh
sources.author: Newberry Library
sources.verified_by: ChatGPT direct institutional research guide read
sources.access_note: Guide gives broader 1700–1715 window, notes earlier sixteenth-century predecessor as probable, and emphasizes distinct oral/literary transmission. Same holding institution; not independent chronological confirmation.

sources.citation: Library of Congress, Popol Vuh: Transcription in Quiché Mayan and Translation into Spanish, https://www.loc.gov/item/2021668226/
sources.author: Library of Congress
sources.venue: World Digital Library / Library of Congress
sources.access_note: LOC reproduces partner metadata and gives [1700 to 1703]; not independent manuscript dating.

does_not_demonstrate: These dates do not mark the origin of the K'iche' Maya religious tradition.
The broad and narrow catalog intervals should not be reported as a precise proven moment of copying.
An early modern manuscript does not date the emergence of the underlying mythic motifs.
adversarial_counter: The Newberry research guide uses the broader interval 1700–1715, so even reputable institutional descriptions differ in precision.
notes: Source-based audit: draft awaiting independent review. The existing Tradition entity's 1701–1703 year range is more precise than the catalog entries checked in this pass; reconcile without presenting a founding year.
